answer:
Recommendation: don't ship on Monday and don't report "13% uplift" yet.
1) Peeking: the analyst checked daily and stopped B the first day p fell below 0.05. That optional stopping inflates the false-positive rate well above 5%, so p = 0.041 is not a valid significance level. Run the planned 14 days or use a proper sequential test.
2) Multiple comparisons: three variants vs control. With a Bonferroni correction the threshold is 0.05/3 ≈ 0.0167, and 0.041 fails.
3) Sample ratio mismatch: control has 10,950 users while the variants have ~10,020–10,180 (expected ~10,300 each). A chi-square SRM test flags this; there is likely an assignment or logging bug, and no result is trustworthy until it is fixed.
4) The 13% is relative (4.30% vs 3.80%); the absolute lift is 0.5 pp — exactly the MDE — with a wide confidence interval.

case_material: Meridian Logistics (US, 1,100 employees) must eliminate 40 roles in its operations division of 400 people. case_material: A rural health clinic is adding a battery to its rooftop solar system so that critical loads (vaccine refrigerator, lighting, communications) run through the night.
